question.problem:
A drone has positive velocity $v(t)$ after being flown upward from an initial height of $0$ feet at time  $t=0$ seconds. The velocity of the drone is recorded for selected values of $t$ over the interval $0\le t\le 40$ seconds, as shown in the table below. 

| $t\,\text{(seconds)}$ | $0$ | $7$ | $15$ | $25$ | $32$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v\,\text{(feet/second)}$ | $3$ | $10$ | $25$ | $40$ | $46$ | $49$ |

Use the right Riemann sum over $[0,40]$ with five subintervals to approximate the total distance covered by the drone.

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the velocity-time graph.*

current_example.problem:
The following table shows the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[1,4].$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $3.5$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0$ | $4$ | $8.5$ | $10$ | $8$ |

Use the right Riemann sum, with the four subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[1,4].$
current_example.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=4$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is computed as 

$$
\mathcal{A}	\approx	f(2)\Delta x_1+f(3)\Delta x_2+f(3.5)\Delta x_3+f(4)\Delta x_4,
$$

where each $\Delta x_i$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
\Delta x_i = x_{i}-x_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a table of values that include the $\Delta x$'s.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $3.5$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\Delta x$ | $-$ | $1$ | $1$ | $0.5$ | $0.5$ |
| $f(x)$ | $-$ | $4$ | $8.5$ | $10$ | $8$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈4\cdot 1+8.5\cdot 1+10\cdot 0.5+8\cdot 0.5 \\  & =4+8.5+5+4 \\  & =21.5.\end{aligned}
$$
